# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# fields: COMMAND_RPC_RELAY_TX::response_t, src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server_commands_defs.h:970-977
#         -> ONE key, `tx_hash` (std::string). NO status/untrusted.
# request: { hex string } (:960-967) -- and `hex` is NOT a raw transaction blob. It is hex of a
#         SERIALIZED wallet2::pending_tx: on_relay_tx parses it into a tools::wallet2::pending_tx
#         (src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server.cpp:1914-1943). That is what `transfer` returns in
#         tx_metadata, never tx_blob. See transfer-do-not-relay.json.
# `tx_hash` MATCHES transfer-do-not-relay.json's tx_hash BYTE FOR BYTE, which is the happy path of
#         DESIGN.md §2a.9: send::relay compares the returned tx_hash with the BuiltTx.txid it
#         recorded, and on a mismatch refuses to mark the entry relayed, exits 1 with
#         reason: txid_mismatch and raises send_may_be_in_flight.
# WHAT THAT CHECK PROVES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT (§2a.9, and §2j does not let a check be described as
#         stronger than its mechanism): wallet-rpc computes this hash LOCALLY from the metadata blob
#         it was just sent -- res.tx_hash = pod_to_hex(get_transaction_hash(ptx.tx)) (:1963), the
#         same function `transfer` used at :1216-1221. A mismatch therefore means fmonero relayed the
#         wrong entry of a sweep's tx_metadata_list: a real bug, and the ONLY bug this check can
#         catch. It is NOT evidence that the daemon accepted the transaction -- that evidence is
#         relay_tx returning at all, because it calls commit_tx, which throws and becomes
#         -4 GENERIC_TRANSFER_ERROR on daemon rejection (:1952-1961).
# relay_tx IS REFUSED IN RESTRICTED WALLET MODE (:1905-1910), which is one more reason DESIGN.md
#         §4.2 never puts --restricted-rpc on the wallet unit.
# relay_tx-mismatch.json (--scenario mismatch) is the fixture that makes the §2a.9 comparison fail.
